claim_boundary: Daily OHLC patterns and high-low information can contain market-state information, but neither broad equity evidence nor range-based microstructure estimators establish that a Bitcoin close near its daily high predicts robust DRA economics. Exactly one separately frozen equal-capital historical screen may therefore falsify whether close location distinguishes unresolved directional persistence from intraday rejection at an unchanged positive-momentum DRA entry. Failure closes the exact family without tuning; success only retains a prior for one separately frozen hypothesis.

feature_contract.formula: the final hourly close minus the complete UTC-day low, divided by the complete UTC-day high minus low, then divided by the median of exactly the prior 20 complete UTC-day close-location values

prior_matrix.finding: Large-sample tests report that some multi-day open-high-low-close price patterns contain out-of-sample information in historical US equities.
prior_matrix.identity: Caginalp and Laurent, The Predictive Power of Price Patterns (1998)
prior_matrix.transfer_boundary: Multi-day equity candlestick evidence does not validate a one-day Bitcoin close-location feature, its direction, normalization, threshold or DRA profit effect.

prior_matrix.finding: Daily high and low prices encode both variance and bid-ask-spread effects, showing that range position can inherit microstructure noise as well as price information.
prior_matrix.identity: Corwin and Schultz, A Simple Way to Estimate Bid-Ask Spreads from Daily High and Low Prices (2012)
prior_matrix.transfer_boundary: The high-low range is not pure directional demand; spread, sampling and venue effects can create apparent close-location structure without tradable alpha.

prior_matrix.finding: Range-based estimators can carry information not present in close-to-close volatility alone, while their empirical predictability is estimator- and market-dependent.
prior_matrix.identity: Petnehazi and Gall, Exploring the Predictability of Range-Based Volatility Estimators Using RNNs (2018)
prior_matrix.transfer_boundary: Volatility-estimator predictability is not return predictability and does not establish persistence rather than reversal after a high close location.

real_time_design_requirements: Use exactly the 24 hourly OHLCV bars wholly inside the latest complete UTC day and no preceding or later bar.
Compute close location as final close minus daily low divided by daily high minus daily low; require a strictly positive range and retain the value in the closed interval from zero to one.
Divide the latest complete-day close location by the median of exactly the prior 20 complete-day values.
Keep the DRA parent, positive-momentum direction, lot cost, capacity, exits, fee, adverse slippage, cooldown and fill clock unchanged.
Freeze primary 1.0 and neighbors 0.8 and 1.2 before outcome access; do not search a different relation, absolute cutoff, lookback, candle definition or threshold.

Require every V1 economic, annual breadth, holding and neighbor gate plus strict Design and Validation realized-PnL improvement, non-worse underwater duration and non-increased terminal inventory under V2.
Do not describe the feature as order flow, open post-2024 OOS or create a candidate from this prior audit.
uncertainty: Close location is mechanically related to the day's extrema and may proxy volatility, spread, path or sampling effects rather than directional persistence.
The DRA parent already requires positive 24-hour momentum, so the feature may be redundant and may have too few independent interventions.
A positive total-PnL screen could still come from suppressed losing inventory; V2 therefore requires realized improvement and explicit underwater and terminal-inventory non-inferiority.
No pre-2025 feature outcome, post-2024 evidence, OOS, candidate, runtime filter or Trading path was accessed or authorized while freezing this prior.
